target.title: Add customizable provider confetti palettes
target.body:
# Provider-branded celebrations CodexBar now uses a small, provider-specific color palette when it celebrates a usage reset. --- ## The Problem I liked CodexBar’s reset confetti, but every provider used a newly randomized rainbow. A Claude reset looked essentially the same as a Codex, OpenAI, or Deepgram reset. I wanted each celebration to feel connected to the provider while keeping configuration optional. --- ## Root Cause After I brought the issue to Codex, we traced the reset path together. ScreenConfettiOverlayController generated six random colors every time it ran. ProviderBranding stored one display color for each provider, but it had no provider-specific confetti palette. The underlying Vortex animation already accepted explicit colors. The missing pieces were the palette data and the wiring from the provider descriptor to the overlay. --- ## Scoping and Blast Radius We considered three approaches: keep one shared palette, add a user-facing color picker, or assign a researched palette to every provider automatically. We chose the provider-palette approach because it creates a recognizable result with no required setup; users can optionally override it locally. The functional change stays inside the existing reset celebration path and its optional local palette-editor path. It does not change usage calculations, reset detection, provider fetching, authentication, refresh schedules, or the setting that enables confetti. The larger-looking part of the diff is mechanical: all 59 provider descriptors need to supply the new required palette. --- ## Implementation We researched all 59 providers individually, using the provider’s exact identity. Official logos and brand material were preferred; in-product or terminal colors were used only when clearer brand guidance was unavailable. The two providers added to main after the original implementation were reviewed with the same methodology. - ProviderBranding.confettiPalette requires every provider descriptor to supply two or three colors. - When a reset occurs, playLimitResetConfetti resolves the provider and passes its palette into the existing Vortex animation. - Tests cover default-palette behavior, local override persistence, and malformed or incomplete user input. - Each provider’s default palette sits beside its descriptor, keeping future additions explicit and small. The current branch keeps the same split: provider-specific palettes are in commit 433ea2a, and local palette preferences are in ce3045ce. --- ## User Acceptance Testing Dave ran the new build as his normal CodexBar for two days. Branded confetti worked as expected, and he reported no new issues. We also triggered representative warm, cool, monochrome, and neon palettes—Claude, Codex, OpenAI, and Deepgram—and checked them against both a neutral background and Dave’s normal desktop. --- ## Outcome Reset celebrations now identify the provider automatically while preserving the existing animation, placement, timing, click-through behavior, and user setting. ### Neutral background

Claude — terracotta, cream, and near-black
Codex — blue-violet and lavender

OpenAI — black, gray, and white
Deepgram — green, blue, and near-black
### Normal desktop

Claude
Codex

OpenAI
Deepgram
Every clip contains 65 frames and runs for 4.34 seconds. The desktop versions use fully opaque frames so the browser cannot expose a different page or wallpaper color between frames. --- ## Remaining Scope New providers need a two- or three-color palette in their descriptor when they are added. Users may override defaults locally from the provider Settings page; this contribution deliberately keeps that editor lightweight and local-only. --- CodexBar contribution notes prepared for the provider-branded celebrations pull request.

target.title: [security] Fix upstream monitor script injection
target.body:
## Summary

This PR prevents external upstream commit summaries from being interpreted as JavaScript by the scheduled upstream-monitor workflow.

- pass all `steps.check.outputs` values to `actions/github-script` through `env`
- read the values from `process.env` inside the script
- preserve the existing issue body, update logic, pinned actions, and least-privilege token permissions

## Why this matters

The workflow fetches the independently controlled Quotio repository and includes recent commit subjects in an automatically managed CodexBar issue. Those subjects were interpolated directly into JavaScript template literals before `actions/github-script` parsed the script.

A commit subject containing a backtick could therefore terminate the intended template literal and inject JavaScript into the scheduled workflow. The action receives the workflow's authenticated GitHub client with `issues: write` access.

Passing the values through environment variables keeps them as data instead of executable source.

## Affected code

- `.github/workflows/upstream-monitor.yml`
- `Create or update issue` step

## Root cause

Untrusted step outputs were embedded directly into the `github-script` source:

```yaml
const quotioSummary = `${{ steps.check.outputs.quotio_summary }}`;
```

GitHub expands the expression before the JavaScript is parsed, so JavaScript-significant characters in an upstream commit subject could change the generated program.

## Repro conditions

- an attacker-controlled commit subject reaches the monitored Quotio default branch, for example through a squash-merged contribution
- the scheduled or manually dispatched upstream-monitor workflow observes that commit
- the commit summary is inserted into the `github-script` source

## Steps to reproduce

A safe synthetic regression used a commit-summary string containing a backtick and a harmless assignment. Under the old source-concatenation shape, the assignment executed. Under this patch, the same string is read from `process.env`, remains inert, and is preserved in the generated issue body.

No real GitHub token, issue, credential, or external repository was modified during validation.

## Impact

Injected code runs with the workflow's existing permissions:

```yaml
permissions:
  issues: write
  contents: read
```

This can affect issue integrity and availability, including issue creation, modification, comments, labels, and state changes. The explicit permission block prevents direct source or release modification.

## CVSS assessment

- Score: **5.4 (Medium)**
- Vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L`
- CWE: CWE-94 / CWE-95

## Suggested fix

Implemented here: move all step-output expressions to the action's `env` mapping and consume them through `process.env`. This avoids constructing JavaScript source from externally influenced data.

## Validation

- `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo rhysd/actionlint@sha256:b1934ee5f1c509618f2508e6eb47ee0d3520686341fec936f3b79331f9315667 -color -shellcheck= .github/workflows/upstream-monitor.yml`
- Docker Node 24 regression: crafted summary remained inert data and remained present in the generated body
- structural regression: confirmed the `github-script` block contains no direct `steps.check.outputs` interpolation and reads all six values through `process.env`
- `git diff --check`

`make check` reached the repository lint stage but the downloaded SwiftLint binary could not load `sourcekitdInProc.framework` in this Command Line Tools-only environment. `make test` was also blocked before project tests ran because the local toolchain could not import the Swift `Testing` module. These failures are environment/toolchain setup issues and do not touch the workflow-only change.

## Disclosure status

This PR contains the complete fix and bounded impact description. No credentials or live exploitation were used.

target.title: fix: show StepFun credit-plan usage instead of false 0%
target.body:
## Summary

StepFun credit-based subscription plans (e.g. Mini, Pro — `plan_family: 2`) report usage through `plan_credit_rate_limit.subscription_credit_left_rate`, not the 5-hour/weekly rate windows. For these plans the API returns `five_hour_usage_left_rate: 0` and `weekly_usage_left_rate: 0` (meaning "no rate-limit window configured"), but CodexBar interpreted the `0` as "0% remaining → 100% used", showing a false **0% available** even when 96%+ of the credit remained.

This PR also fixes a secondary issue: the `Oasis-Webid` was hardcoded, so browser-imported (Manual mode) tokens — which carry a different `device_id` — caused `"auth failed: oasis-token is embezzled"` errors.

## Root cause

**`StepFunUsageFetcher.swift`** — `StepFunRateLimitResponse` decoded only the rate-window fields (`five_hour_usage_left_rate`, `weekly_usage_left_rate`) and completely ignored the `plan_credit_rate_limit` / `plan_family` fields. Credit-plan responses were mapped to `(1.0 - 0) × 100 = 100% used`.

Additionally, `webID` was a hardcoded constant. The StepFun Dashboard validates that the `Oasis-Webid` header matches the token JWT's `device_id` claim; a mismatch yields HTTP 401 `"oasis-token is embezzled"`.

## Changes

### `StepFunUsageFetcher.swift`
1. **New response types**: `StepFunPlanCreditRateLimit` and `StepFunPlanCreditBucket` decode the `plan_credit_rate_limit` object (including `subscription_credit_left_rate`, `topup_credit_left_rate`, and `credit_buckets`).
2. **`StepFunFlexibleNumber`** now also decodes JSON-string-encoded numbers (the API returns `credit_total`/`credit_residual` as strings like `"400000000"`).
3. **Credit-plan detection**: `isCreditPlan` checks `plan_family == 2`, with a fallback heuristic (rate fields 0 + reset_time 0 + credit data present).
4. **`toUsageSnapshot()`**: for credit plans, the credit balance becomes the primary window and the meaningless 0%-left rate windows are dropped.
5. **Dynamic `webID(forToken:)`**: extracts `device_id` from the refresh-token JWT payload, falling back to the hardcoded default only during the initial device-registration/login flow.

### Tests (`StepFunUsageFetcherTests.swift`)
4 new test cases:
- `parses credit-plan response and maps credit as primary window`
- `does not treat rate-window plan as credit plan`
- `uses credit buckets when explicit rate is absent`
- `credit plan does not throw when rate fields are missing`

### Docs & changelog
- `docs/stepfun.md`: documented the credit-plan response format and usage mapping.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: added a Fixed entry under 0.43.1.

## Before / After

**Before** (Mini plan, 96.4% credit remaining):
```
== StepFun (web) ==
5h Window: 0% left [------------]
Resets now
```

**After**:
```
== StepFun (web) ==
5h Window: 96% left [===========-]
Resets in 25d 13h
Plan: Mini
```

## Commands run

```bash
swift build --product CodexBarCLI          # ✅ compiles
swift test --filter StepFun                # ✅ 34/34 pass
swiftformat Sources/.../StepFunUsageFetcher.swift Tests/.../StepFunUsageFetcherTests.swift
```

target.title: fix(tasks): key cancel button state by taskId to match the cancel action
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Tasks page and chat background-task rail used different identifiers for one cancellation interaction:

- the Cancel action passes `task.taskId` and the in-flight set is keyed by that cancellation identifier;
- the renderers previously queried the set with `task.id`.

The wire schema permits these values to differ, so a client receiving `{ id: "row-id", taskId: "cancel-id" }` could send the correct cancellation request while failing to disable the matching button or show its pending state.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** pending-state lookup used row identity (`id`) while the action/state owner uses cancellation identity (`taskId`).
- **Fix:** both renderers query `cancellingTaskIds.has(task.taskId)`, matching the value passed to `onCancel`.
- **Best owner boundary:** row/DOM identity remains `task.id`; action identity remains `task.taskId`. The fix does not collapse protocol fields or duplicate ID translation in controllers.

The current core Gateway projection emits equal values for these fields, so this is protocol-permitted client consistency hardening rather than a claim that today's core Gateway routinely produces divergent IDs.

## User Impact

When a protocol-valid task has distinct row and cancellation IDs, the Cancel button now immediately disables and shows the pending state during the `tasks.cancel` round trip. Tasks with equal IDs behave exactly as before.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

**Terminal capture from a GitHub-hosted Node 24 + Playwright Chromium run using the real Control UI `/tasks` route, a deferred `tasks.cancel` response, and deterministic mocked Gateway data:**

```text
BEFORE: tasks.cancel sent { taskId: "cancel-id" }; button remained enabled with "Cancel"
AFTER:  tasks.cancel sent { taskId: "cancel-id" }; button disabled with "Cancelling…"
Playwright assertions: passed
```

### UI before/after screenshots

- Proof run: https://github.com/miorbnli/openclaw/actions/runs/29400428645
- Screenshot artifact: https://github.com/miorbnli/openclaw/actions/runs/29400428645/artifacts/8336903133
- Files: `tasks/before-task-cancelling.png`, `tasks/after-task-cancelling.png`

target.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged
target.body:
Closes #107980

### What Problem This Solves
The per-identity control-plane write budget is hardcoded at 3 requests per 60s
(`src/gateway/control-plane-rate-limit.ts`). That default is right for interactive
clients, but trusted automation legitimately bursts past it: a fleet provisioner
applying one `config.patch` per customer during a rollout is throttled to one write
every ~48 seconds, serializing the whole operation.

### Why This Change Was Made
Adds `gateway.controlPlaneWritesPerMinute` (integer, range 1–600, default 3 — existing
behavior unchanged). The 60s window and per device|IP bucket keying are untouched,
so every caller stays individually bounded. The value is read from the required live
runtime-config accessor on each request. Its reload rule is `hot`: reload-enabled
gateways publish the updated runtime snapshot, while reload-disabled gateways report
and schedule the required restart instead of persisting a value that cannot become
active. The rate-limit error reports the effective configured limit. Help text and both
doc pages state explicitly that raising the value applies to every identity on the
gateway.

### User Impact
Operators running trusted write-bursting automation (provisioners, fleet controllers)
can tune the budget; everyone else sees identical behavior and an unchanged default.

### Evidence
- *Production validation:* we operate a multi-tenant OpenClaw fleet where a
  provisioner applies one `config.patch` per customer during blue/green rollouts.
  Under the stock 3/60s budget those writes throttle to ~1 per 48s, serializing
  rollouts at ~48s per customer; with a raised per-identity budget (carried as a
  fork patch since June, this dial's ancestor) full rollouts complete with zero
  rate-limit rejections and no observed write-storm side effects.
- Unit: configured max is honored, default stays 3/60s, and the resolver reads
  `gateway.controlPlaneWritesPerMinute`
- Dispatch: config-driven limit end to end, dynamic `"5 per 60s"` error detail, and
  separate bounded budgets for two client identities
- Reload policy: hot classification publishes the new runtime snapshot; reload-off
  `config.patch` coverage proves a direct restart is required and scheduled
- Contract: all request contexts exercised by control-plane writes provide the required
  runtime-config accessor, including plugin-HTTP suspension dispatch
- Config: schema accepts 60 and rejects 0, 1.5, and 601; label and FIELD_HELP entries
- 289 focused tests green across rate limiting, config validation/reload, config-write
  restart policy, and suspension dispatch
- Fresh automated review found no remaining actionable regression after the reload-mode
  and required-context fixes

target.title: fix(heartbeat): use fresh Date.now() for schedule advance after runOnce (#104951)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After ~24h uptime, heartbeat scheduler fires rapid-fire cycles (1-min intervals instead of configured cadence like 30m). The pattern is: 3 healthy cycles → rapid burst → self-recovery or stuck.

The `run()` function captures `const now = startedAt` once at the beginning, then uses that same stale `now` for `advanceAgentSchedule()` AFTER `runOnce()` completes. When `runOnce()` takes significant wall-clock time (network delays, GC pressure after 24h uptime), `computeNextHeartbeatPhaseDueMs({ nowMs: staleNow })` returns a phase-aligned `nextDueMs` that's already past → `Math.max(0, nextDue - Date.now()) = 0` → immediate refire → feedback loop.

## Fix

Use `Date.now()` at each post-`runOnce()` `advanceAgentSchedule()` call site so the next schedule is computed from actual completion time. This is consistent with how `Date.now()` is already used in `scheduleNext()` itself.

### Changes

- **`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`**: 4 call sites changed (`now` → `Date.now()`)
  - Targeted path success (line 1500)
  - Targeted path error catch (line 1508)
  - Fan-out path error catch (line 1530)
  - Fan-out path success (line 1542)
- **`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`**: New test "recomputes next due from current time after slow runOnce to prevent cadence decay"

### What is NOT changed

- `recordRunBookkeeping(agent, now)` — correctly records run START time for cooldown
- `advanceStaleScheduleAfterDeferral(agent, now, ...)` — no runOnce has run yet at that point
- The pre-runOnce due check `now < agent.nextDueMs` — correct to check at run start time

## Evidence

New test validates the fix:
```typescript
it("recomputes next due from current time after slow runOnce to prevent cadence decay (#104951)", async () => {
  // Simulates runOnce taking 20s wall-clock time via vi.setSystemTime()
  // Verifies: after slow run, next heartbeat does NOT fire within 5s (no 0ms rearm)
  // Verifies: next heartbeat DOES fire after a full interval
});
```

The test uses `vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + slowRunDurationMs)` inside the mock `runOnce` to simulate wall-clock time passing, then asserts no premature refire (which would happen with the stale `now` bug).

Diff is minimal (4 one-word changes + 1 test):
```
 src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts | 34 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts                |  8 +++----
 2 files changed, 38 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

Closes #104951

target.title: improve(diagnostics): surface run startup phases as session-correlated events
target.body:
Closes #107981

### What Problem This Solves
The embedded runner reports ordered startup milestones (workspace, auth,
context_engine, …, model_call_started) through the private `onExecutionPhase`
callback, so they reach typing indicators and cron watchdogs but never the diagnostic
bus. External status surfaces that already consume `run.attempt` / `run.progress` /
`model.call.*` cannot see where a turn is during startup — exactly the window that
matters when a run hangs before its first model call. The phase enum's own contract
comment says "external status surfaces and diagnostics consume the formatted values";
this puts the values where diagnostics can reach them.

### Why This Change Was Made
One wrap at the runner entry (`withExecutionPhaseDiagnostics`) emits a
session-correlated `run.execution_phase` event (runId, required sessionId, optional
sessionKey, closed `EmbeddedAgentExecutionPhase`, provider/model/tool context) for every
transition. The event rides the async diagnostic lane like the other high-frequency
lifecycle events (ordering vs `model.call.*` preserved; no subscriber work on the hot
path). The wrapper tracks session rotation via `onSessionIdChanged` so post-compaction
phases carry the current session id. Stability records project into their dedicated
phase/provider/model fields.

### User Impact
In-process diagnostic-bus consumers (plugins, status dashboards, and
stability/support surfaces) gain turn-startup visibility with a closed, typed phase
contract. No new OTLP metric or span exporter is added; the diagnostics-otel switch
acknowledges the typed event for exhaustive handling. Existing consumers are unchanged;
the event is additive and process-gated like its siblings.

### Evidence
- *Production validation:* our deployment has consumed exactly this signal (as a
  fork patch, `session.execution_phase`, since 2026-05-18) to drive a live
  "now doing X" phase cursor in a production status UI — two months of
  continuous operation across daily agent runs, with no observed emitter overhead or
  event-loss issues.
- The phase vocabulary is closed at 14 values, but values can repeat across retries and
  multiple model/tool-loop calls. Events use the existing 10,000-entry async queue with
  100-event drain batches.
- 5 wrapper tests: emit+forward, no-callback emit, async-lane ordering after
  `model.call.started`, session-rotation regression, disabled-process silence
- 50 focused tests green across the wrapper, diagnostic bus, and stability projection
- Comprehensive changed-surface gate green: Plugin SDK API/export/surface checks, core
  and extension production/test typechecks, lint, boundaries, and runtime guards
- Docs: opentelemetry.md diagnostic event catalog entry; diagnostics-otel exhaustive
  switch case acknowledged without claiming OTLP export
- Privacy: the event carries identifiers and names only (phase, provider, model,
  tool name) — never payloads or prompt content

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. target.title: fix(shared): block prototype-polluting keys in JSON schema default hydration
target.body:
## Summary
A plugin whose manifest `configSchema` declares a `__proto__` property can pollute `Object.prototype` process-wide the moment its config is validated. Plugin config validation hydrates JSON Schema defaults automatically for every discovered plugin, so no operator action beyond loading the plugin is required. After the malicious plugin loads, every plain object in the process carries the attacker-supplied property.

## Root cause
`src/shared/json-schema-defaults.ts`, `applyObjectPropertyDefaults`. The property-defaults loop iterates schema-controlled keys and dereferences the matching value slot with no blocked-key guard, unlike the codebase's centralized `isBlockedObjectKey` used at other untrusted object-write boundaries.

Plugin manifests arrive as parsed JSON, so a `__proto__` entry in `properties` is an own key that `Object.entries` yields. For a config value with no own `__proto__`, `value["__proto__"]` reads the inherited `Object.prototype`, and the nested default hydration then writes defaults straight onto it.

before:
```ts
for (const [key, propertySchema] of Object.entries(properties)) {
  const currentValue = value[key];
  const defaultedValue = applySchemaDefaults(
    propertySchema as JsonSchemaValue,
    currentValue,
    ...
  );
  if (defaultedValue !== currentValue || currentValue === undefined) {
    if (defaultedValue !== undefined) {
      value[key] = defaultedValue;
    }
  }
}
```

## Fix
Skip blocked keys (`__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor`) at each write site in `applyObjectPropertyDefaults`, reusing the existing `isBlockedObjectKey` helper from `src/infra/prototype-keys.ts`.

after:
```ts
for (const [key, propertySchema] of Object.entries(properties)) {
  if (isBlockedObjectKey(key)) {
    continue;
  }
  const currentValue = value[key];
  ...
}
```

## Why this is the right boundary
`applyObjectPropertyDefaults` is the single function that writes default values into a caller-supplied object using schema-derived and value-derived keys, and it routes every plugin/SDK default-hydration call (`applyJsonSchemaDefaults` -> `applySchemaDefaults`). Guarding its three write loops here fixes the vector for every caller rather than at one call site. The `properties` loop is the live global-pollution path (the added regression test fails on pristine `main`); the `patternProperties` and `additionalProperties` loops key off own value keys so they do not globally pollute today, but guarding all three keeps the whole function consistent with `isBlockedObjectKey` usage elsewhere and prevents the vector from reappearing under refactoring. Legitimate config keys named `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` are unrepresentable through a prototype chain anyway, so skipping their default hydration changes no valid behavior.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/json-schema-defaults.test.ts src/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/infra/prototype-keys.test.ts` passes (17 tests).
- New `applyJsonSchemaDefaults prototype safety` case fails on pristine `main` (`expected 'yes' to be undefined`) and passes with the patch.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/shared/json-schema-defaults.ts src/shared/json-schema-defaults.test.ts` clean; `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` clean.
- `tsgo` on the changed files reports no new diagnostics (unrelated pre-existing module-resolution errors from broken workspace symlinks in the local checkout are not touched by this diff).

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a plugin manifest `configSchema` with a `__proto__` property pollutes `Object.prototype` for the whole process during ordinary plugin config validation.
Real environment tested: drove the real plugin config validation builder `buildJsonPluginConfigSchema(...).safeParse({})` from `src/plugins/config-schema.ts` (the same call the plugin loader makes on a discovered plugin), on pristine `origin/main` abfdfd65 and on the patched tree with an identical manifest configSchema; the real default-hydration path, the real TypeBox validation, and the real `Object.prototype` stayed live, nothing mocked.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `./node_modules/.bin/tsx` on a driver that builds the plugin config schema from the manifest JSON and calls `safeParse({})`, then reads a freshly created object.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main abfdfd65)
safeParse.success: true
Object.prototype.polluted: pwned
freshObject.polluted: pwned
verdict: PROTOTYPE POLLUTED process-wide
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
safeParse.success: true
Object.prototype.polluted: undefined
freshObject.polluted: undefined
verdict: prototype clean
```
Observed result after fix: validating the same plugin manifest leaves `Object.prototype` and newly created objects free of the attacker property, while config validation still succeeds.
What was not tested: no live end-to-end plugin discovery from disk was exercised (the real config-schema builder was driven directly with the manifest JSON); full repo build was not run.

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): classify model calls as client spans
target.body:
Closes #102017

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators exporting OpenTelemetry traces would see model-provider calls classified as `INTERNAL` unless they enabled the experimental GenAI semantic-convention shape. That hid outgoing model dependencies in trace backends and made provider latency harder to distinguish from in-process work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-call span kind was coupled to `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`, even though that setting should control span naming and provider attributes rather than whether a model request is a client operation. This change keeps model-call spans `CLIENT` in both legacy and experimental naming modes.

Generic tool-execution spans deliberately remain `INTERNAL`: the shared event represents local reads, writes, processes, and remote tools without carrying a reliable remote-execution signal. This follows the scope requested when #102041 was closed and avoids misclassifying local work.

The public OpenTelemetry docs and configuration reference now describe that boundary explicitly.

## User Impact

Trace backends can consistently classify model-provider calls as outgoing client operations without requiring an experimental environment setting. Existing dashboards that filter model spans by `INTERNAL` may need to include `CLIENT`; runtime behavior, configuration, and exported span names are otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` — 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-otel-smoke.e2e.test.ts` — 28 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Pre-commit Codex autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings.

The regression assertion proves default model-call spans receive `SpanKind.CLIENT` while generic tool spans continue omitting an explicit kind and therefore remain `INTERNAL`.

Ran the diagnostics service from exact PR head `6bbfbd0678e4dfec96438a570a0332da5a4c294f` against a real preloaded `NodeTracerProvider` with `SimpleSpanProcessor` and `ConsoleSpanExporter`. `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` was explicitly unset. target.title: fix(plugins): remove incorrect modifying hook timeout fallback in getClaimingHookTimeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getClaimingHookTimeoutMs` in `src/plugins/hooks.ts:499-504` is a copy-paste of `getModifyingHookTimeoutMs` but incorrectly kept the `modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook` dictionary as its fallback. Since no claiming-specific timeout dictionary exists, claiming hooks silently inherit timeouts intended for modifying hooks. For example, a `before_agent_run` timeout of 10s (intended for modifying hooks) would also apply to claiming hooks using the same hook name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix removes the erroneous fallback to `modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook`. Only `hook.timeoutMs` (the per-registration timeout) is used for claiming hooks, which is the intended behavior — claiming hooks should use their own explicit timeout or have no timeout at all.

## User Impact

- Before: Claiming hooks could inherit timeouts from `modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook` entries, potentially causing claiming hooks to time out with an incorrect timeout
- After: Claiming hooks only use their own `hook.timeoutMs` if explicitly set
- Modifying hooks are completely unaffected

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** getClaimingHookTimeoutMs uses modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook as fallback
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24, commit `dccd10fd0` on branch `fix/claiming-hook-timeout-dictionary`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node /tmp/verify-claiming-timeout.mjs` — standalone script simulating both buggy and fixed logic against various hook names and timeout configurations
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  [BUG CONFIRMED] buggy(before_agent_run) = 10000 — incorrectly fell back to modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook
  [PASS] fixed(before_agent_run) = undefined (expected: undefined) — claiming hook should NOT inherit modifying timeout
  [BUG CONFIRMED] buggy(reply_sending) = 5000 — incorrectly fell back to modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook
  [PASS] fixed(reply_sending) = undefined (expected: undefined) — claiming hook should NOT inherit modifying timeout
  [BUG CONFIRMED] buggy(session_claim) = 30000 — incorrectly fell back to modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook
  [PASS] fixed(session_claim) = 30000 (expected: 30000) — explicit timeout should be respected
  [BUG CONFIRMED] buggy(session_claim) = undefined — incorrectly fell back to modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook
  [PASS] fixed(session_claim) = undefined (expected: undefined) — no timeout = undefined in both
  [BUG CONFIRMED] buggy(before_agent_run) = 20000 — incorrectly fell back to modifyingHookTimeoutMsByHook
  [PASS] fixed(before_agent_run) = 20000 (expected: 20000) — explicit timeout overrides modifying default
  Verdict: PASS (0 failures)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Claiming hooks no longer inherit modifying hook timeout defaults
- **What was not tested:** Full test suite and build (requires pnpm install), CI will cover

## Tests and validation

## What Problem This Solves

`isExtensionFile` in `src/plugins/discovery.ts:299` only filters `.d.ts` files but not `.d.mts` or `.d.cts` declaration files. `path.extname('.d.mts')` returns `.mts`, so these declaration files pass all extension checks and are treated as valid plugin entry points. ESM projects using modern TS declaration file variants may experience unexpected plugin loading errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix belongs in `isExtensionFile` because it is the single gate for extension file filtering. The old `endsWith('.d.ts')` check was too narrow for the TS declaration file family. Using a regex `/\\.d\\.[cm]?ts$/` covers all three variants without changing the function signature or callers.

## User Impact

- Before: `.d.mts` and `.d.cts` files in plugin directories are mistakenly treated as valid plugin entries
- After: All TS declaration file variants (.d.ts, .d.mts, .d.cts) are correctly excluded
- Non-declaration .ts, .mts, .cts files are unaffected

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** .d.mts and .d.cts declaration files not filtered in extension discovery
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24, commit `b0c93e331` on branch `fix/d-cts-d-mts-extension-filter`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node /tmp/verify-extension-filter.mjs` — standalone verification script that tests both old (buggy) and new (fixed) patterns against a matrix of declaration and non-declaration file extensions
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text

  [PASS] types.d.mts -> true (expected: true) — .d.mts should be declaration
  [PASS] types.d.cts -> true (expected: true) — .d.cts should be declaration
  [PASS] index.ts -> false (expected: false) — .ts should not be declaration
  [PASS] index.mts -> false (expected: false) — .mts should not be declaration
  [PASS] index.cts -> false (expected: false) — .cts should not be declaration
  [PASS] foo.test.ts -> false (expected: false) — .test.ts should not be declaration
  [PASS] bar.d.tsx -> false (expected: false) — .d.tsx should not be declaration
  [PASS] .d.ts -> true (expected: true) — bare .d.ts should be declaration
  [PASS] Old pattern correctly rejects .d.mts (proving the bug exists)
  [PASS] Old pattern correctly rejects .d.cts (proving the bug exists)
  Verdict: PASS (0 failures)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All declaration file variants correctly detected as non-extension files; non-declaration files unaffected
- **What was not tested:** Full plugin discovery integration test (requires pnpm install), CI will cover

## Tests and validation

New test `ignores TypeScript declaration files (.d.ts, .d.mts, .d.cts) in extension roots` added to `src/plugins/discovery.test.ts` covering the three declaration variants in an integration-style discovery. No type signature changes, so build is deferred to CI.

- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes — affects plugin discovery; only reduces false positives (was incorrectly accepting files, now correctly rejecting)

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve authored file-reference links
target.body: Closes #105679 ## What Problem This Solves Telegram's Markdown formatter treated any authored link whose visible label matched a supported file-like hostname as if it came from MarkdownIt's automatic linkifier. For example, `[README.md](https://README.md)` was indistinguishable from a plain `README.md` reference and the authored anchor was silently replaced with `README.md`. The supported suppression extensions currently include `.md`, `.go`, `.py`, `.pl`, `.sh`, `.am`, `.at`, `.be`, and `.cc`. `.ts` is not in that set, so `main.ts` is not a valid before/after reproducer for this bug. ## Why This Change Was Made Markdown Core now keeps MarkdownIt's `linkify` provenance as private renderer metadata instead of adding a field to the public `MarkdownLinkSpan` contract. The fact is copied through clamping, slicing, table transforms, render-boundary splitting, and render-aware chunk coalescing. `renderMarkdownWithMarkers` exposes only a renderer-specific `{ origin: "authored" | "linkify" }` context while evaluating a link. Telegram suppresses a file-like link only when that context says it came from MarkdownIt's `linkify` rule. Markdown/IR output then wraps remaining plain file references without trying to infer provenance again from rendered anchors. Explicit Markdown links therefore remain anchors, while the public raw-HTML helper keeps its default defensive de-linkification behavior because raw HTML does not carry trustworthy parser provenance. The branch was rebuilt on current `main` after the Markdown IR and Telegram renderer refactors, removing the prior merge conflict and picking up the upstream fixes for the two unrelated CI failures seen on the previous head. ## User Impact Intentional Telegram links whose labels resemble supported file names keep their destinations, while plain file references such as `README.md` continue to render as code and avoid unwanted registrar previews. Existing direct-HTML compatibility behavior is preserved. ## Evidence - Head: `0d6ac6385ca8f5538a31e2fb3a8f58c1de2ad937`. - `git diff --check` passed. - Focused Markdown Core coverage checks public span shape plus renderer provenance through parsing/clamping, slicing, and table rendering. - Telegram formatter coverage checks authored-link preservation for a supported `.md` label, automatic file-reference suppression, mixed authored/plain output, chunked output, the Bot API 10.2 rich-block path introduced on current `main`, and existing raw-HTML de-linkification behavior. - Post-rebase hosted CI run [`29411581760`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29411581760) is fully green: 53 successful jobs, 12 scope skips, and no failures. This includes `check-test-types`, `check-dependencies`, lint/format, the plugin SDK surface budget, every Node test shard, build artifacts, prod types, guards, and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. - The previous head's two unrelated failures were fixed upstream by #107987 (`session-history-state` test typing) and #107977 (serialized hooks process bootstraps); rebasing picked up both fixes. - Initial Mantis run `29396726601` showed that `main.ts` has no baseline/candidate delta because `.ts` is not a supported suppression extension. - Corrected Mantis run `29401877063` passed against baseline `ad1071bcd0` and candidate `9be0456f81`. The [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105911#issuecomment-4978225456) contains paired native Telegram Desktop screenshots, GIFs, and MP4s; the evidence manifest marks both lanes `pass`, candidate `fixed: true`, and overall `pass: true`. - The Mantis proof job itself succeeded, including manifest validation, artifact upload, and PR evidence publication. The workflow's red conclusion comes only from a separate `Clear Mantis command reaction` cleanup job receiving a 403 while removing the eyes reaction.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing delete-side ownership guard in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-shared.ts` was generalized into `pluginRuntimeSessionMismatchError` / `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it reports the action (`delete` or `patch`). `sessions.patch` now runs the check before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again through an `authorize` callback inside `applySessionPatchProjection`, so authorization happens against the authoritative transaction-selected row before any projection is persisted.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `src/gateway/server.sessions.patch-plugin-ownership.test.ts` (new, 4 tests): owned mutation allowed; foreign-owned archive and unarchive rejected; legacy ownerless row rejected (fail-closed upgrade boundary); concurrent-create race rejected against the transaction-selected row; `pluginOwnerId` stamped when patch creates a new session.
- Unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Exact head: `9305961be4b1dabd64afbddddf0c6c100c175763` (rebased onto `upstream/main` `851f76cb0d07`).
- Focused local runs on the exact head (Node 24.15.0):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.sessions.patch-plugin-ownership.test.ts` → 4 passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 81 passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → 103 passed, 1 failed (`sessions.delete removes clean session worktrees…`; host `/usr/bin/git` is 2.27 and lacks `git init -b`; test and helper untouched by this PR, green on CI).
- `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors and `oxfmt --check` clean on all 7 changed files.

## Real behavior proof

Deployed-gateway trace on the exact head: a real gateway process (worktree `dist` build, stamp head `9305961be4b`) with isolated `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, loopback bind, random ports, token auth, and a mock OpenAI provider (`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`), no real credentials. Two temporary bundled proof plugins (`sessions-patch-proof-alpha` / `-beta`) were loaded by the normal plugin loader and called `sessions.patch` through the trusted in-process plugin-runtime path (`api.runtime.gateway.request`), driven over real WebSocket RPC via `openclaw gateway call`:

- Plugin patches a session it owns → succeeds; newly created rows are stamped with the caller's `pluginOwnerId`.
- Plugin patches a session owned by another plugin → `INVALID_REQUEST` ("did not create it"); the foreign row is unchanged.
- Plugin patches a legacy ownerless row → `INVALID_REQUEST` (fail closed); a non-plugin operator client can still create and patch that row.

Full redacted transcripts, persisted SQLite before/after state, and test output are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103534#issuecomment-4983631786. Remaining before merge: explicit maintainer approval of the intentional fail-closed ownerless-row compatibility boundary (P1), plus coordination with the sibling sessions.create ownership PR #103148.

target.title: fix(matrix): use sliceUtf16Safe in chunkTextForOutbound to prevent surrogate pair splitting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chunkTextForOutbound` in `extensions/matrix/runtime-api.ts` uses bare `.slice(0, N)` to split outgoing Matrix message text into chunks. When the text contains multi-byte UTF-16 characters such as emoji or CJK, the slice can land in the middle of a surrogate pair, producing corrupted characters visible to the end user.

This was identified during a defensive programming audit of UTF-16 safe truncation patterns (category 4 in the security checklist).

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing code uses `remaining.slice(0, limit)` which operates on UTF-16 code units. A high surrogate at position `limit-1` followed by a low surrogate at `limit` gets split into two invalid standalone surrogates, corrupting the output.

The fix replaces all three `.slice(0, N)$ call sites with `sliceUtf16Safe`, which detects surrogate pair boundaries and adjusts the cut point to avoid splitting them.

`sliceUtf16Safe$ is already available through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-runtime` and is the established codebase-wide pattern for this use case.

## User Impact

Matrix outbound messages containing emoji (😊, 🎉, 👋), CJK characters (中文, 日本語), or other supplementary-plane Unicode will no longer display with corrupted/garbled characters after chunking.

## Evidence

- 42/42 existing tests pass
- The SDK-level shared equivalent (`chunkTextByBreakResolver` in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts`) already uses `avoidTrailingHighSurrogateBreak` — this brings the Matrix extension inline with that protection
- `sliceUtf16Safe` has its own dedicated test suite in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts`

target.title: fix(whatsapp): use canonical media primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where WhatsApp maintained local copies of outbound media loading, audio transcoding, MIME classification, and base64 decoding even though canonical media owners already existed. The copies had drifted: injected media readers could silently widen local-file access, image optimization was not exposed through the SDK facade, and malformed base64 uploads could reach permissive decoding.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves WhatsApp onto the canonical media paths and deletes its local outbound loader. The shared APIs gain only additive, typed capabilities: outbound loading forwards the existing image-optimization option, audio transcoding supports a typed Ogg/Opus container and maximum duration, and media-core exposes strict base64 source parsing. Existing transcode defaults remain unchanged.

WhatsApp-specific behavior stays local: MP3, M4A, and WebM voice inputs still transcode; Ogg/Opus remains the only direct voice-compatible form; document naming remains transport-specific; and the legacy retry helper is intentionally untouched.

## User Impact

Supported WhatsApp media sending and voice-note behavior remain the same. Injected media readers must now provide an explicit local-root boundary, malformed base64 and data URLs are rejected consistently, and oversized uploads are rejected from their encoded-size estimate before allocating the decoded buffer.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): repair interrupted tool calls at provider-bound replay seam
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted sessions (process crash, /new, or network drop during tool execution) leave orphaned tool_use blocks in persisted session history, causing Anthropic API to reject every subsequent resume with a persistent 400 error. Call the existing provider-aware `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` in the provider-bound replay path to synthesize error tool_results for missing pairs.

- Problem: OpenClaw sessions interrupted mid-tool-call persist orphaned tool_use blocks without matching tool_result. Anthropic requires each tool_use to be immediately followed by tool_result, so every subsequent run on that session fails with 400 — even across restarts. The existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback (in `tool-result-context-guard.ts`) only covers ongoing tool-result replay, not initial session resume.
- Solution: Gate `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` behind `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` in `attempt.ts` at the two `buildSessionContext().messages → agent.state.messages` assignment points. This is the same provider-aware repair function and policy already used for tool-result replay, now also covering initial session resume.
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` (2 call sites wrapped with policy-gated repair, 0 net LOC growth).
- What did NOT change: `session-manager.ts` (untouched), `session-transcript-repair.ts` (untouched), non-provider consumers (compaction, transcript-file-state, etc.), the existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106781
- Related to #106935 (concurrent PR by xydigitLybnnnn — targets session-manager.ts unconditionally)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a session is interrupted mid-tool-call (crash, /new, network drop), the session history in openclaw.sqlite retains a dangling `tool_use` block with no matching `tool_result`. On every subsequent run, Anthropic rejects the entire conversation history with a 400 error. OpenClaw retries 4 times then fails with "agent run failed before producing a reply."

The repair function chain (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` → `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) was already integrated into the tool-result replay path via `repairAssembledMessages` in `attempt.ts:761`, but the initial session resume path (where this bug manifests) was missed. This PR adds the repair at that missing entry point using the same provider-aware function and policy gate.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Orphaned tool_use blocks from interrupted sessions are repaired with synthetic error tool_results during initial provider-bound session resume.
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, PR head commit `6e445b00cd9` (rebased onto latest `origin/main`).
- Unit tests: `attempt-session-boundary.test.ts` (7/7 pass, including new `"applies repair to orphaned tool_use when policy is enabled"`) + `attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts` (3/3 pass, including new `"applies repair to orphaned tool_use when policy is enabled"`).

target.title: Create Claw agent and root install record
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the second [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328):

- Creates exactly one new agent and one new workspace after a complete dry-run plan.
- Requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>` for mutation, rebuilds the plan in the mutating invocation, and rejects stale consent before any write.
- Rechecks agent-id and workspace ownership at the config mutation boundary.
- Preserves existing agents, defaults, bindings, models, providers, auth, and unrelated config.
- Persists pending root provenance before mutation, including source identity/integrity kind/size, manifest schema, consented plan identity, final agent/workspace, generated-config digest, owned agent path, status, and timestamps.
- Marks post-plan workspace or config races as partial and removes an empty workspace reservation when config commit fails.
- Returns versioned `openclaw.clawAddResult.v1` results with the consented plan identity.

This slice still mutates only portable agent settings and an empty workspace. Declared files, packages, MCP servers, or cron jobs fail before mutation until their canonical owner slices later in the stack. No declared component is skipped.

## Lifecycle

```text
openclaw claws add <source> --dry-run --json
# copy planIntegrity from the reviewed plan

openclaw claws add <source> --yes --plan-integrity <digest> --json
```

Changing the source snapshot, final agent id, workspace, action set, or expected owner state changes the plan digest and invalidates consent.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- This PR: consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- Next: [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) confined workspace files and managed hashes

## Validation

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/schema-conformance.test.ts \
  src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts

  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

git diff --check

```

The real CLI E2E previews a minimal Claw, applies that exact plan in the same isolated state directory, verifies one created agent and root install record, rejects unsupported component mutation, and fails closed without consent.

target.title: fix(signal): reject hex/exponent text-style span offsets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container sends could apply the wrong styled span when `text-style` start/length tokens used JavaScript-only forms such as `0x10` or `1e1`. Those tokens were coerced with `Number(...)` into different offsets, so bold/italic markers could land on the wrong characters or invent spans that the caller never intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse `text-style` `start`/`length` at the canonical Signal container translation boundary (`containerRpcRequest` → `/v2/send`) with the same `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper already used for container quote timestamps. The parser lives in `client-container-text-style.ts` so oversized `client-container.ts` stays LOC-neutral.

Boundaries: no config keys; no native signal-cli path; incomplete `start:length:style` entries still drop the same way.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `path:extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts` and `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger text-style` — **0** competing PRs. Open Signal PRs #101380 / #100906 do not touch `text-style` `Number()` parsing.

## User Impact

- **Before:** `0x10:4:ITALIC` silently styled offset 16; `1e1:2:BOLD` silently styled offset 10; fractional lengths like `1.5` were accepted.
- **After:** Non-decimal tokens are dropped (same drop path as incomplete entries). Ordinary decimal spans such as `0:4:BOLD` are unchanged. All-invalid lists omit `text_mode=styled` and keep the plain message.

target.title: fix(update): reject npm redacted global root paths
target.body:
## Summary

npm >= 11 can redact UUID-like global-root path segments as literal `***`. Treating that output as a real path can create a literal `***` directory tree during staged updates while leaving the live install stale.

This revision:

- rejects `***` only for npm root probes, preserving legal pnpm paths;
- rejects multiline package-manager root output;
- applies the same parser to install-target resolution and manager detection;
- verifies the composed update flow never stages into or passes a poisoned root to npm.

Fixes #107239

## Test evidence

Two-sided regression proof:

- current upstream base + new tests: 3 expected failures (redacted npm root, composed poisoned staging path, multiline output);
- previous PR head + new tests: 2 expected failures (legal pnpm `***` path rejected, multiline output accepted);
- corrected candidate: 57/57 focused tests pass.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"
# Owner is "claude" — cross-agent confirmed ✓
```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓
- Before fix: label was written to `main_assistant` store → silently lost ✗

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` passes `maxOptions: 20` explicitly to `normalizePollInput`
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, reject 21)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and `buildPollStartContent(..., { maxOptions: 20 })`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.
- **P1: Provide real behavior proof (not only unit tests)** — Added a runtime trace that drives the real production boundaries for both the 20 (accepted) and 21 (rejected) paths. See "Runtime behavior trace" below.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now enforced at the Matrix boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Real production modules executed — the core outbound `normalizePollInput` boundary (the exact call at `src/infra/outbound/message.ts:510` and `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts:1021`) and the Matrix `buildPollStartContent` m.poll.start builder, plus Vitest regression tests.

### Runtime behavior trace

Drove the real production paths for both the 20-option (success) and 21-option (rejection) cases, with `maxOptions` sourced from the Matrix outbound `pollMaxOptions = 20`. Captured output:

```text
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(20, maxOptions=20) -> options.length=20
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(21, maxOptions=20) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(20) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20, last id=answer20
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(21) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
```

- 20 options: accepted end to end; the Matrix builder emits 20 `m.poll.start` answers (`answer1`..`answer20`).
- 21 options: rejected at the normalize boundary with the real runtime error `Poll supports at most 20 options`, on **both** the core outbound path and the Matrix builder path.

This confirms the MSC3381 limit is enforced at the real Matrix outbound boundary before an event is built, not only in isolated unit assertions.

- **Exact commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/polls.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # src/polls.test.ts — 7 passed
  - "does not limit options when maxOptions is omitted" → 50 options accepted ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 10 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "rejects more than 20 poll options per MSC3381" → throws "at most 20" ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts — 6 passed
  - "declares a 20-option poll maximum..." → outbound.pollMaxOptions = 20 ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary. Public helper contract preserved (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + runtime boundary trace
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 rejected (protocol boundary in `buildPollStartContent`)
  - Matrix outbound: `pollMaxOptions = 20` declared on static adapter
  - Public helper: omitted `maxOptions` does not limit (contract preserved)

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Matrix outbound adapter did not declare `pollMaxOptions`, unlike all other poll channel adapters (Discord, WhatsApp, MS Teams, Telegram).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No Matrix-owned poll option limit enforcement.

target.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts
target.body:
Closes #92043

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a legitimate multi-chunk compaction could hit the safety timeout after completing earlier chunks, discard that completed work, and restart from chunk one on every retry. Affected sessions could remain stuck in a repeated compaction failure loop even though useful partial progress already existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction pipeline now preserves completed chunks or completed stages when later work is interrupted specifically by the wrapper-owned safety timeout. This includes all completed stage inputs when final merge times out before its first request, a completed history stage when a following split-turn prefix starts with a timeout, and the last successful quality attempt when its retry starts with a timeout. Partial progress carries the exact completed-message range back to the compaction preparation, so `firstKeptEntryId` moves only past summarized entries and every unsummarized message remains in active context. Entry IDs are mapped in the actual post-repair summarization order, including when late tool results are moved next to their tool calls; synthesized or otherwise unalignable messages make the partial path fail closed instead of advancing an unsafe boundary.

The safeguard returns a typed partial result, and `AgentSession` may persist it only while the same timeout error's bounded settlement token remains open. The wrapper signal is passed into only its own compaction invocation, so a queued timeout cannot cancel an active or auto compaction in the same session. The internal `startCompaction()` result exposes the accepted commit separately from that invocation's lifecycle completion, while public `compact()`, extension `onComplete`, and `compaction_end` retain their existing full-lifecycle semantics. The embedded owner drains completion within a bounded post-commit grace on both wrapper success and rejection. If a `session_compact` hook still does not finish, the compaction session is invalidated, disposal becomes idempotent, and late completion cannot reconnect it; the lane therefore remains safe without becoming permanently blocked.

External caller aborts, plugin-owned compaction timeouts, failures before any chunk completes, unmarked results, and results arriving after the settlement window remain terminal. The default timeout and public config shape are unchanged; the preflight failure reply still points users to `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` when repeated timeouts require a larger configured budget.

This intentionally permits one typed partial result to commit after safety-timeout cancellation during the bounded settlement window. Final acceptance of that post-timeout session-state policy remains a compaction owner decision.

The branch was rebased onto the recorded main snapshot used for this repair. Main had already removed the former Pi runtime consumer of `src/node-host/with-timeout.ts`; this patch migrates the remaining embedded compaction caller to the reason-owned settlement wrapper. Repository-wide search then found no TypeScript caller, so the unused helper and its sole test are deleted.

## User Impact

Long-running sessions can retain already summarized context instead of repeatedly losing all compaction progress and restarting the same work. Messages not covered by that partial summary remain verbatim in active context. If compaction still cannot settle within the bounded window, users receive the existing terminal failure behavior and actionable timeout guidance.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

On current candidate head `0fe148a0ddc71a8bd42388a7a8d75cbc73e829f6`, a Linux Node 24.15.0 run used a loopback OpenAI-compatible streaming server and exercised production summary generation, chunk planning, timeout cancellation, provider stream closure, safeguard marking, `AgentSession` persistence, and context rebuild.

```json
{
  "provider_requests": 2,
  "completed_chunks_before_timeout": 1,
  "total_chunks": 2,
  "interrupted_provider_request_closed": true,
  "safeguard_marked_partial_result": true,
  "persisted_compaction_entries": 1,
  "first_kept_entry_matches_unsummarized_message": true,
  "rebuilt_context_contains_partial_summary": true,
  "persisted_entry_contains_partial_summary": true,
  "rebuilt_context_retains_unsummarized_message": true
}
```

The proof observed two real streaming provider requests. The first chunk completed, the second request was canceled by the wrapper-owned safety timeout, exactly one typed partial compaction was persisted, `firstKeptEntryId` advanced only to the first unsummarized entry, and context rebuild contained both the partial summary and the unsummarized message. It used a 1-second safety timeout and 3-second settlement window to exercise the same production ownership path without waiting the default 180 seconds; it did not call a third-party provider.

### Current rebased candidate

Validated on Linux with Node 24.15.0:

```text
compaction-partial-summary.test.ts: 13 passed
compaction.identifier-preservation.test.ts: 6 passed
embedded-agent-runner.compaction-safety-timeout.test.ts: 29 passed
compaction-safeguard.test.ts: 110 passed (including repaired-order retained boundary)
compact.hooks.test.ts: 111 passed (including accepted/rejected bounded lifecycle cleanup)
agent-session-compaction-timeout.test.ts: 6 passed (including public lifecycle/event ordering and no reconnect after disposal)
sessions/sdk.test.ts: 22 passed

core production typecheck: passed
core test typecheck: passed
type-aware lint across all live changed TypeScript files: passed
oxfmt --check across all live changed TypeScript files: passed
plugin SDK surface check: passed
Knip dependency and unused-export checks passed before the lifecycle review fixes; later changes added only used internal lifecycle seams, did not change dependencies, and the current plugin SDK surface check passed

```

The broad changed-test unit-fast shard also exposed failures in unmodified current-main surfaces: four system-run tests now reject `/bin/sh -c /bin/ls` under the current interpreter-binding policy, and one auth-doctor test timed out. This PR has no diff in those files or their owners; the directly affected suites above pass.

target.title: fix(plugins): treat path-like provider ids as no bundled policy surface (#103744)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103744.

`sessions_list` (and any other request path that resolves provider policy — `sessions_spawn`, status) crashed with `Error: Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: my-ngc:nvidia` whenever a session referenced a model from a custom provider whose derived provider id contains `:` or `/`. NGC-style model ids (`org/model`) make this deterministic: `parseModelRef` splits `my-ngc:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` at the first `/`, deriving provider `my-ngc:nvidia`, and that string flowed into `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface` → `loadBundledPluginPublicArtifactModuleSync({ dirName: providerId })` → `normalizeBundledPluginDirName`, which throws on path-like values.

The core defect: a provider id is not necessarily a bundled-plugin directory name, but the policy lookup treated every provider id as one and let the validation error escape on request paths. `normalizeProviderId` only lowercases, so the `:`/`/` survive.

### Change

- `src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.ts`: extract the existing validation into an `isBundledPluginDirName` predicate; `normalizeBundledPluginDirName` keeps throwing for actual loader misuse.
- `src/plugins/provider-public-artifacts.ts`: `tryLoadBundledProviderPolicySurface` returns null for ids that cannot name a bundled plugin directory — custom providers simply have no bundled policy surface. The security-relevant validation still guards every real path resolution.

The mis-parse of `provider:org/model` references in `parseModelRef` is a separate, adjacent question (that colon syntax is only a compat alias for `openrouter:auto` today); this PR fixes the crash at the owner boundary so no provider id shape can take down `sessions_list`.

## Verification

- New regression (written first, confirmed failing on main with the exact reported error): `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface("my-ngc:nvidia")`, `("z-ai/glm-5.2")`, and `("..")` return null instead of throwing.
- `pnpm test src/plugins src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 2,685 passed. The 3 failures (`plugin-registry-snapshot`, `sdk-alias`) fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (verified via `git stash` baseline run) and are unrelated.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `sessions_list` crashes with "Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: <provider>:<namespace>" for sessions referencing custom-provider models with `org/model` ids.
Real environment tested: the real `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface` production path with the exact provider id from the issue repro (`my-ngc:nvidia`), driven through the existing provider-public-artifacts test harness against the real bundled plugin registry.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test src/plugins/provider-public-artifacts.test.ts src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/public-surface-loader.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: before the patch the new test fails with `Error: Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: my-ngc:nvidia` (the issue's exact error); after the patch all 28 tests in the three touched suites pass and the lookup returns null.
Observed result after fix: policy lookup degrades to "no bundled surface" for path-like provider ids; valid bundled providers (openai, minimax, moonshot smoke tests) still resolve their surfaces.
What was not tested: an end-to-end `sessions_list` call against a live gateway with an NGC proxy provider configured; the crash site is fully covered at the resolver boundary that every such request path shares.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Current head: `32452922d779597437621cdf63fb02d740b49837`.
- Dependency contract checked in Crabbox source: config files load before environment overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` overrides the configured provider, and an explicit CLI `--provider` remains the final override.
- Claude via acpx independently routed the policy cases correctly: env `local-container` -> local Docker proof with no explicit provider; unset env -> Blacksmith fallback; untrusted credential-hydrated Testbox request -> sanitized AWS or secretless CI.
- A second Claude/acpx audit read all four active policy surfaces and found no remaining mandatory-Testbox or eager-prewarm contradiction. The mandatory hosted Testbox check in `scripts/pr prepare-run` is a merge-gate verification contract, not provider selection.
- Claude via acpx ran a real inherited-provider command with no explicit `--provider`: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_b5d22ebde587 --no-sync --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts`.
- Wrapper output: `provider=local-container`, lease `cbx_b5d22ebde587`, local Docker proof, 195/195 tests passed, exit 0. Cleanup verified: container removed and lease status returned not found.
- `oxfmt --check AGENTS.md .agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md .agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md`
- `git diff --check`
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head GitHub checks are pending.
